Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

cause verb

make something happen

also bring about, make happen, be the cause of, give rise to, lead to, generate

classical

Varr. RR 1.12.2: efficiunt difficilīs morbōs
Caes. BG 4.29.1: quī diēs maritimōs aestūs maximōs in Ōceanō efficere cōnsuēvit

efficiō, efficere, effēcī, effectum

verb, third conjugation (-iō): with an accusative, or ut and the subjunctive

bring about, cause

What is caused goes in the accusative, or in an ut-clause (efficere ut, Cic. Lael. 59, Lewis & Short); with a second accusative it is “make”: fortūna eōs efficit caecōs (Cic. Lael. 54, Lewis & Short). Traupman (p. 288) also gives facere ut: quid fēcit ut abīret?, what caused him to leave?

Other words

  • afferō, afferre, attulī, allātum — bring on, cause (pain, worry, delay)

    verb, irregular · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 1: pācem, tranquillitātem, ōtium, concordiam (Lewis & Short)

    Of what a thing brings on someone, with the dative: illī molestiam adfert, it brings him trouble (Ter. Hec. 344).

  • moveō, movēre, mōvī, mōtum — stir up, cause (laughter, pain, a war)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Phaedr. 1 prol. 3: quod rīsum movet; Traupman 63, 288

    Of feelings and bodily states: rīsum, lacrimās, dolōrem movēre.

  • pariō, parere, peperī, partum — give rise to, breed

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. And. 68: vēritās odium parit

  • causa esse — be the cause (of)

    phrase: causa with the genitive of what is caused, or cūr · also used · classical · Liv. 1.13.3: nōs causa bellī … sumus; Cic. Phil. 9.7: is quī causa mortis fuit (Lewis & Short)

  • in causā esse — be the cause, be to blame

    phrase: with ut or quō and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Liv. 40.26.5: vim morbī in causā esse, quō sērius perficerētur; Quint. 12.5.2 (Lewis & Short)

    Rare, and not before Livy (Lewis & Short). The Ciceronian example Lewis & Short gives, Fam. 1.1.1 in causā haec sunt, means “in the case, things stand as follows”.

Examples

  • crēscunt animālia quaedam minūta, quae nōn possunt oculī cōnsequī, et per āera intus in corpus per ōs ac nārēs perveniunt atque efficiunt difficilīs morbōs

    certain tiny creatures breed that the eye cannot follow; they get into the body through the air, by the mouth and nose, and cause serious illnessesVarr. RR 1.12.2

  • nōs causa bellī, nōs volnerum ac caedium virīs ac parentibus sumus

    it is we who are the cause of the war, we who cause our husbands’ and fathers’ wounds and deathsLiv. 1.13.3

  • obsequium amīcōs, vēritās odium parit

    going along with people makes friends; the truth makes enemiesTer. And. 68

See also create, involve, result, effect, happen.
